name: Czechia: Prague, Český Krumlov, Brno, Kutná Hora, Olomouc

cities.base: The northern edge of the Old Town by Josefov: five minutes to the clock and Charles Bridge, and a notch quieter than the main square.
cities.name: Prague

cities.base: Inside the old town loop or on Latrán below the castle: everything is under 10 minutes on foot, and after the tour buses leave at 17:00 the streets empty.
cities.name: Český Krumlov

cities.base: Near Zelný trh and the Old Town Hall, between Špilberk and the station: all walkable, with the Bib Gourmand places in the streets off the square.
cities.name: Brno

cities.base: Most people day-trip from Prague. If you stay, sleep by Palackého náměstí, a walk from St Barbara's; the Sedlec Ossuary is 1.5km north.
cities.name: Kutná Hora

cities.base: Between Horní and Dolní náměstí: the fountains, the cathedral and the Denisova restaurant row are all within 10 minutes on foot.
cities.name: Olomouc

places.name: Prague Castle
places.note: Founded around 870 and 570m long, the largest ancient castle complex anywhere, with 2.59 million visitors in 2024. The grounds are free from 06:00; circuit buildings run 09:00 to 17:00 (16:00 Nov to Mar), so be at the gate at 09:00. Gardens shut Nov to Feb.

places.name: St. Vitus Cathedral
places.note: Entry is on the Castle circuit ticket, so check the price when you buy it. Sundays it opens 12:00, last entry 20 minutes before close, 16:00 in winter. The Wenceslas chapel is seen from the doorway; the new 5,755-pipe organ was finished June 2026.

places.name: Charles Bridge
places.note: 516m of bridge built 1357 to 1402, pedestrian since 1965, with about 30 statues, most of them replicas now. Cross it at or before 07:00; by 09:00 it is shoulder to shoulder.

places.name: Old Town Hall Tower & Astronomical Clock
places.note: The clock went in in 1410 and the apostles parade hourly 09:00 to 23:00. Watch from the tower, not the crowd: 350 CZK for tower and hall, half price in the first hour after opening, lift 4 euros extra. Jan to Mar it runs 10:00 to 19:00.

places.name: Vyšehrad
places.note: The other castle hill, a 10th-century fort turned park. Park and cemetery are free and open round the clock; 10:00 to 18:00 is the casemates. Dvořák, Smetana and Mucha are buried here, and the river view beats the Castle's for a fraction of the crowd.

places.name: Žižkov Television Tower
places.note: A 216m Communist-era transmitter with David Černý's ten bronze babies crawling up the legs. The deck at 93m gives the one panorama without this tower in it; 14 euros, open to midnight with last entry 23:00, so go after dark.

places.name: Jewish Town (Josefov synagogues)
places.note: One 600 CZK ticket, good for 3 days, covers six synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery; allow 2 to 3 hours. Closed Saturdays and Jewish holidays (Sep 13, 21, 27 and Oct 4 in 2026). To 19:00 May to Aug, 16:30 from Oct 18.

places.name: DOX Centre for Contemporary Art
places.note: A converted Holešovice factory with rotating contemporary shows and Gulliver, a 42m airship, sitting on the roof. 330 CZK and closed Mondays; walk back through Letná afterwards.

places.name: Náplavka Farmers' Market
places.note: Saturdays, February to December: 90-plus stalls of cheese, fish, mushrooms and pastries on the riverbank. Get there by 09:00, then walk 5 minutes to U Kalendů for lunch. If a river event is on, it moves to Palackého náměstí.

places.name: Prague Botanical Garden, Fata Morgana greenhouse
places.note: Fata Morgana is a 130m greenhouse in three climate zones, and the garden adds a working vineyard and a Japanese garden. 180 CZK, 15% less online. The greenhouse is closed Mondays and shuts 16:00 Nov to Feb; Troja Château is next door.

places.name: Speculum Alchemiae
places.note: An alchemist's workshop found under Haštalská after the 2002 floods, said to tunnel to the Castle. Guided 30-minute tours on the half hour in small groups, 200 CZK; it fits between Josefov and the Old Town Square.

places.name: Letná Park & Metronome
places.note: A working metronome stands on the plinth of a demolished 1955 Stalin monument, above a beer garden with the best free Castle view in town. Walk ten minutes west past it for real quiet.

places.name: Eska
places.note: Karlín's all-day bakery kitchen, all fermenting, wood fire and fire roasting. Order the sourdough and an open sandwich. Weekends it opens 09:00 and it closes at 19:00, so this is breakfast or lunch, not dinner.

places.name: U Kalendů
places.note: Bib Gourmand 2025, an old Podskalí tavern brought back with its own bakery. Order the contemporary Czech classics and do not skip the bread. On a Saturday, do Náplavka market first; it is 5 minutes up the embankment.

places.name: Alma
places.note: Bib Gourmand 2025: open kitchen, natural wine, its own coffee roaster and a backyard wine garden, good from breakfast to a nightcap. Sundays it runs 17:30 to 22:00, and the wine bar side is shut Sunday and Monday.

places.name: Výčep
places.note: Bib Gourmand 2025, Wallachian-leaning Czech cooking deep in residential Vinohrady: house sourdough, their own cured meats and sauerkraut, five taps of Dalešice beer. Sundays 12:00 to 22:00. No tourists.

places.name: Na Kopci
places.note: Ten Bib Gourmands running since 2015, French-Czech cooking off the tourist map in Anděl. Come at lunch, when the specials (schnitzel, lasagna, Caesar) are 230 to 320 CZK.

places.name: U Matěje
places.note: Bib Gourmand in Dejvice, the embassy quarter, where tourists do not go. Meat from their own smokehouse, Austro-Hungarian sauces and big plates for the middle of the table, so come with three or four and share.

places.name: Hemingway Bar
places.note: The widest absinthe list in the country and a regular on world best-bar lists, with a small kitchen doing fish and Italian pastries. It is tiny: book for Friday or Saturday, when it runs to 02:00.

places.name: Riegrovy Sady Beer Garden
places.note: 1,200 seats at the top of the park, Pilsner Urquell for about 3 dollars and the Castle skyline behind you. Opens 12:00 at weekends. The locals' Letná: same view, fewer people.

places.name: Český Krumlov Castle & Tower
places.note: Second in size to Prague Castle, founded 1253, UNESCO since 1992. The two interior routes, the Tower and the Baroque Theatre are separate tickets with their own hours, so pick one and check the price first. The Tower runs 09:00 to 16:30.

places.name: Castle Gardens
places.note: Formal gardens a level up from the courtyards, free, 07:00 to 19:00 May to Sep and to 17:00 in October, shut all winter. The crowd thins here, so walk up straight after the castle.
places.neighborhood: Above the castle, past the Cloak Bridge

places.name: Cloak Bridge & Bear Moat
places.note: A five-storey covered bridge from 1764 over a moat that still keeps live bears. Free to cross, and the most photographed view in town is from the far side; come before 11:00 or after 17:00, outside the coach-tour hours.

places.name: Baroque Castle Theatre
places.note: One of a handful of 18th-century theatres left with the original machinery, sets and costumes. Guided tours on the hour (10:00, 11:00, 13:00, 14:00, 15:00 from Sep 21 to Oct 31) with few places: book ahead and check the price. Other months, hours vary, check.

places.name: Museum Fotoatelier Seidel
places.note: The Seidel family's 1905 studio and darkroom, kept as working rooms, seen on a 50-minute audioguide. Closed Mondays and 12:00 to 13:00 for lunch, last tour an hour before close; check the price at the door.

places.name: Egon Schiele Art Centrum
places.note: Schiele lived here until the town drove him out over his models; the centre holds a serious permanent Schiele collection plus modern shows, the one real gallery in town. Its hours page was down when checked: hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Náměstí Svornosti (Old Town Square)
places.note: The plague column and town hall, and every walking route starts here; the whole old town is under 500m across. Come back after 17:00, when the day-trippers have gone and the town is yours.

places.name: Vltava canoe and raft rental (Malecek)
places.note: No licence or guide needed; about 25 dollars covers boat, paddles, vests, dry bags and transport, and the short run floats you right under the castle. Roughly April to October, as the river is too cold and high Nov to Mar. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Wooden raft river cruise
places.note: The no-paddling version: a guided 50-minute float through town on a wooden raft, with commentary, about 15 dollars. A good first look at the castle from river level, in season; hours vary, check.

places.name: Křížová hora (Cross Mountain)
places.note: A pilgrimage chapel on the hill above town, and the one high view that takes in the castle and the river bend together, without the Cloak Bridge crowd. A real uphill walk, 90 minutes there and back.

places.name: Krčma v Šatlavské ulici
places.note: A medieval cellar with meat spit-roasted over open fires beside the tables. In every guide and still good; order whatever is on the spit. It is always full, so reserve. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Papa's Living Restaurant
places.note: The one Krumlov locals also eat at: Mediterranean-leaning plates and a real wine list, less staged than the taverns. Phone bookings are taken 09:15 to 24:00; hours vary, check.

places.name: Nonna Gina
places.note: Wood-fired pizza, the one non-Czech dinner locals recommend. Summer evenings book up, so reserve; hours vary, check.

places.name: Kolektiv
places.note: The breakfast locals use before the tour buses: local free-range eggs cooked to order, gluten-free options. Breakfast is 08:00 to 11:00; later it pours Czech and Austrian wine and prosecco, hours vary, check.

places.name: Krčma Markéta
places.note: The other spit-roast tavern, up by the castle gardens away from the square: the same grilled meat as Šatlavská with a shorter wait. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Apotheka
places.note: Krumlov's one proper cocktail bar, in an old pharmacy. In a town where most places shut by 21:00 or 22:00, this is the evening. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Špilberk Castle
places.note: A 13th-century hill fort the Habsburgs turned into a political prison: the casemate cells, a lookout tower over the city and the Brno City Museum. 50 to 280 CZK by circuit. Some sources say it shuts Mondays Oct to Mar; hours vary, check.

places.name: Cathedral of St Peter and Paul (Petrov)
places.note: Twin 81m neo-Gothic towers you see from all over town. The noon bells ring at 11:00, for a legend of the Swedish siege, and there is a crypt below. Free to enter, tower climb extra; hours vary, check.

places.name: Old Town Hall Tower
places.note: A 15th-century hall with a crooked spire (the mason's revenge, they say) and a stuffed crocodile, the Brno Dragon, free to see in the entry. The tower is 90 CZK, open to 22:00 Jun to Sep and at weekends Jan to Mar; hours vary by month, check.

places.name: Brno Ossuary (Church of St James)
places.note: Found in 2001 and open since 2012: some 50,000 people's remains under the square, the second-largest ossuary in Europe after Paris. 180 CZK, closed Mondays, last entry 30 minutes before close.

places.name: Capuchin Crypt
places.note: More than 150 Capuchin friars, naturally mummified, laid out on the floor of a crypt the order still uses. Stranger than the Ossuary. Apr to Oct 09:00 to 18:00, Nov to Mar 10:00 to 16:00, shorter on Sundays; check the price.

places.name: Villa Tugendhat
places.note: Mies van der Rohe's steel and onyx house of 1929 to 1930, UNESCO-listed. Tours are 200 to 550 CZK and sell out moments after release online; no walk-ins, so book weeks ahead. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Zelný trh (Vegetable Market)
places.note: A vegetable market running since 1190, the oldest in Central Europe, round the Baroque Parnas fountain. Come in the morning; the cellar labyrinth under it is a separate ticket. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Labyrinth under the Vegetable Market
places.note: Over 1,000m of medieval storage cellars 6 to 8m below Zelný trh, open since 2011, with a mock alchemist's lab and old wine cellars. About 6 dollars; hours vary, check.

places.name: Moravian Museum (Dietrichstein Palace)
places.note: The second-oldest and second-largest museum in the country, on Zelný trh. Go for the Venus of Věstonice, a figure over 20,000 years old. About 6 dollars; hours vary, check.

places.name: Punkva Caves (Moravian Karst)
places.note: Caves 40 minutes north, seen partly by boat on an underground river. 450 CZK with the boat, 250 CZK if the water is too high for it. Main season sells out, so reserve. Off-season it is 08:40 to 14:00 and shuts Mondays.

places.name: Brno Reservoir (Brněnská přehrada)
places.note: The city's lake in Bystrc: swimming, kayaks and lakeside walks with a castle across the water. From late May to mid June it launches the Ignis Brunensis fireworks.

places.name: La Bouchée
places.note: French bistro cooking, a step up in price from the Bib places and the one locals name for a proper dinner. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Valoria
places.note: Bib Gourmand: Michal Černý's tasting menus, French, Mediterranean and Far Eastern, with the Moravian wine list first. South of the centre, so make the trip on purpose. Closed Sundays.

places.name: ATELIER bar & bistro
places.note: Bib Gourmand bistro under a glass-roofed courtyard, with vaulted rooms and an open kitchen, a short walk from the Old Town Hall. Lunch after the tower; hours vary, check.

places.name: Borgo Agnese
places.note: Michelin-listed Mediterranean in Staré Brno, with an excavated church wall kept behind glass in the dining room. Order the shrimp confit or the boar with cranberries; hours vary, check.

places.name: Bar, který neexistuje
places.note: The Bar That Doesn't Exist, Brno's best-known cocktail bar: New York speakeasy styling, a big bottle collection, burgers and vegetarian plates. To 02:30 Wed and Thu, 03:30 Fri and Sat; dogs welcome.

places.name: Špalíček
places.note: Czech cooking on the market square: goulash and dumplings at local prices, not square prices. Lunch after the market; hours vary, check.

places.name: Sedlec Ossuary
places.note: The bones of some 40,000 people, arranged by a 19th-century woodcarver into chandeliers, garlands and a coat of arms. The busiest sight in this pack: book online, come early, check the price and the photo rules. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Sedlec Cathedral
places.note: Founded 1142 for the Cistercians and rebuilt after a 1421 fire in the Baroque-Gothic style Bohemia went on to copy. Most skip it for the Ossuary; give it 30 minutes. A joint ticket exists, check the price. Hours vary, check.

places.name: St Barbara's Cathedral
places.note: The 14th-century miners' cathedral, with rare Gothic frescoes of the silver trade that paid for it. Apr to Oct 09:00 to 18:00, shorter in winter, and it shuts early for weddings and concerts; check the price. Approach up Barborská at sunset.

places.name: Hrádek, Czech Museum of Silver
places.note: Tour II puts you in a white coat and helmet and takes you 250m into a medieval silver mine; not for the claustrophobic. Closed Mondays unless a holiday, hours shift by month, last tour 90 minutes before close; check the price.

places.name: Italian Court (Vlašský dvůr)
places.note: The royal mint that struck Bohemia's silver groschen, once a residence of Wenceslas IV. No current figures were published when checked: hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Corpus Christi Chapel
places.note: A former cemetery chapel tucked under Barborská, free, and walked straight past by most people heading for St Barbara's. Hours vary, check.

places.name: GASK Gallery sculpture gardens
places.note: A free sculpture garden looking straight at St Barbara's flying buttresses. Sit here after the cathedral, when the crowd is inside.

places.name: Church of St James
places.note: Romanesque origins from 1165. The tower climb on narrow, uneven steps runs daily May to Sep and at weekends in April and October; check the month and the price. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Barborská Street
places.note: The cobbled lane to St Barbara's, lined with 13 Baroque saints and ending in a valley view. This is the postcard; walk it at sunset, after the day-trip buses leave.

places.name: Old Town and Plague Column
places.note: The 1715 plague column and the Stone, Three Kings, Tyl and Alchemists houses. Mostly pedestrian, and small enough to cross end to end in under an hour.

places.name: Dačický
places.note: The town's name restaurant, medieval-themed with menus drawn from the 16th century. Order the wild boar goulash with gingerbread dumplings; beer garden in summer, fire in winter. Reserve; hours vary, check.

places.name: U Vlašského dvora
places.note: Plain Czech cooking next to the old mint, the less staged version of what Dačický serves. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Piazza Navona
places.note: Pizzeria on the main square, the cheaper dinner when Dačický is booked out, which in season it often is. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Hostinec U Černého kohouta
places.note: The Black Rooster, a plain neighbourhood pub doing Czech standards at local prices, the opposite of the medieval-themed rooms. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Barborská Cocktail and Champagne Bar
places.note: A small cocktail and champagne bar on the postcard street, one of the few places in town for a proper drink rather than beer with dinner. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Vino Kutná Hora wine tasting
places.note: A wine shop and tasting room pouring Czech and Moravian wine by the glass, the sit-down alternative to a pub. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Holy Trinity Column
places.note: A 35m Baroque plague column built 1716 to 1754 and UNESCO-listed since 2000, the largest Baroque sculpture group in Central Europe. Free, at any hour.

places.name: Town Hall & Astronomical Clock
places.note: Rebuilt in 1955 in socialist realism, so workers and athletes parade instead of saints. Be there at noon: the show lasts 7 minutes with a brass cockerel, and the 16 bells now play Czech folk tunes. Free.

places.name: St Wenceslas Cathedral
places.note: Its 100.65m south tower is the tallest in Moravia. The crypt display of vestments and liturgical pieces is open May to Sep. Free; hours vary, check.

places.name: Archdiocesan Museum (Přemyslid Palace)
places.note: In the old Přemyslid palace beside the cathedral: medieval panel paintings, gilded reliquaries and church textiles, about 6 dollars. Do it with the cathedral; hours vary, check.

places.name: Svatý Kopeček Basilica
places.note: A white and gold pilgrimage basilica on a hill 7km northeast, by bus or up a tree-lined path. Free; add the zoo next door for a half day. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Zoo Olomouc
places.note: On the same hill as the basilica, about 10 dollars; walk up, see both, and the afternoon is gone. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Caesar Fountain & Baroque fountains walk
places.note: Six Baroque fountains (Neptune, Hercules, Jupiter, Triton, Caesar, Mercury) plus Arion from 1989, across the two squares. This is Olomouc's real sight, and an hour does it.

places.name: Bezručovy sady
places.note: The park on the old walls above the Morava, with chestnut trees and cherry blossom in spring. Go in April if you can.

places.name: Chrám sv. Mořice (St Maurice Church)
places.note: Gothic hall church holding the country's largest bell, Uligan, cast 1815. The seasonal tower climb looks over both squares; hours vary, check, and check the price.

places.name: Museum of Art Olomouc
places.note: The regional modern-art museum on Denisova, the restaurant street, about 8 dollars, so pair it with dinner. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Long Story Short Eatery & Bakery
places.note: Bib Gourmand bakery, café and hostel in one, cooking all day with its own bakery counter; breakfast here. The kitchen stops 15:00 to 16:00, and Friday and Saturday it runs to 23:00.

places.name: Hanácká hospoda
places.note: Hanák pub cooking on the lower square, a long-running local favourite. Order the fried tvarůžky, the pungent local cheese, if you are going to try it anywhere. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Entrée
places.note: Michelin-listed fine dining, the proper night out in a town built round pub food. Book it for one evening; hours vary, check.

places.name: Svatováclavský pivovar original
places.note: A brewpub with its own beer and a beer spa, where you soak in a barrel of warm beer. The food is solid pub fare; the spa is why people come. Hours vary, check.

places.name: The Keep Cocktail Bar
places.note: The town's standout cocktail bar by local listings, for when you have had enough beer halls. Hours vary, check.

places.name: Moritz microbrewery
places.note: The other brewery pub, on Nešverova, with unfiltered lager on tap. Hours vary, check.

destination.name: Czechia: Prague, Český Krumlov, Brno, Kutná Hora, Olomouc
destination.pitch: Four nights in Prague, then two each in Brno and Olomouc or Krumlov by train, with Kutná Hora as a night or a day. Castles, Gothic churches, bone chapels and Bib Gourmand cooking at pub prices: a culture week, not a nature one.
destination.caveat: Prague's Old Town is a crush by 10:00 and the restaurants on its squares are poor value; eat two streets back. Krumlov fills with day tours 11:00 to 16:00, Brno and Olomouc are 2 to 2.5 hours by train, and Nov to Feb shuts gardens, cuts hours and ends the canoeing. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Prague does the city: Castle hill at 09:00, Letná and Riegrovy beer gardens at dusk, Karlín and Vinohrady for dinner, Hemingway Bar after. Brno is the smaller second city, with Bar, který neexistuje.
because.food: Bib Gourmand cooking at pub prices: U Kalendů, Výčep, Na Kopci and U Matěje in Prague, Valoria and Atelier in Brno, Long Story Short in Olomouc; boar goulash at Dačický, fried tvarůžky at Hanácká.
because.culture: Prague Castle and St Vitus, the six Josefov synagogues, the bone chapels at Sedlec and under St James in Brno, Mies's Villa Tugendhat, St Barbara's in Kutná Hora and Olomouc's UNESCO column.
because.exploration: Go under things: the Brno cellar labyrinth, the Punkva boat caves, 250m of Kutná Hora silver mine, the Speculum Alchemiae. Canoe under Krumlov's castle, or climb Křížová hora for the view back.
